about: Living Roots Wine & Co. was founded in 2016 by Sebastian and Colleen Hardy and makes wine in two hemispheres. Seb comes from six generations of South Australian winemakers; Colleen, a Rochester-area native who left marketing for winemaking, met him while working a vintage in Australia. They make Finger Lakes whites and sparkling wines, starting at Rochester’s only urban winery and now also on Colleen’s family’s Shale Creek Vineyard above Keuka Lake, alongside reds in the Adelaide Hills, and they are known for playful experiments with the region’s grapes.

Red Rizza (“Rizza” is Aussie slang for Riesling) is one of those experiments. After Cabernet Franc grapes were pressed for the winery’s rosé, the Hardys put 100% Riesling juice onto those fresh red skins and let it ferment wild, with native yeasts, borrowing colour, tannin and red-fruit character from the Cabernet Franc. The wine was then aged in old French oak, which adds texture without obvious oak flavour.

The result is neither a white, a red nor a rosé. The winemakers describe Riesling’s citrus and fresh acidity carrying through, joined by darker fruit and soft tannins from the Cabernet Franc skins, with rose petal and cherry. The same curiosity runs through the winery’s Session Gold, which macerates Cayuga White and Vidal on the skins of aromatic hybrid grapes.
facts: 100% Riesling juice fermented on Cabernet Franc skins
Skin-fermented white, light red in colour
